title: pass password store
whyItMatters: The pass password manager keeps one file per site or account, and the file names and folder tree are readable without any key. They reveal every account the person has, even though the passwords themselves are encrypted.
source: pass, the standard unix password manager: stores are kept in ~/.password-store with one .gpg file per entry: https://www.passwordstore.org/
notes: Encrypted with the user's GPG key, so without that private key only names and sizes are exposed. PASSWORD_STORE_DIR can point somewhere else, and pass also writes a .gpg-id file naming the recipients. Other password managers keep their stores elsewhere.

cleanup.exportFirst: Copy the whole password store to an encrypted backup off this computer, and make sure you also hold the GPG key that decrypts it.
steps: Check that the backup opens and that your GPG key is stored somewhere you keep.
Move the folder named in the plan to the Trash and empty the Trash.
cleanup.risk: Removes every saved entry and its history. Without the backup and the GPG key the passwords cannot be recovered. Keep the GPG key for as long as you keep the backup, or the entries stay unreadable.
cleanup.source: passwordstore.org, pass - the standard unix password manager: https://www.passwordstore.org/
